entry.evidence: In fact, there are no studies that use two different methods at the same location to calculate k.

steps.action: Pose the aim: estimate the dust production efficiency k for sandy sediments and compare k from different field methods.
steps.quote: The goals of this study are to determine the dust production efficiency for sandy sediments and to compare results from different methods

steps.action: Take from the literature the expectation that k depends on soil texture and the range of k values for sandy soils.
steps.quote: Studies have found that k is soil texture-dependent

steps.action: Choose two southern Kalahari sites, Spaarwater (bare dune crest) and Kolonkwaneng (interdune), with near-identical sandy texture.
steps.quote: that have very nearly identical sandy textures

steps.action: Deploy two rows of BSNE sediment sampler stems (four heights each) at Spaarwater in 2010-2011 and collect samples monthly; size subsamples for the PM10 fraction.
steps.quote: Big Spring Number Eight (BSNE) sediment samplers were deployed in Spaarwater during the year 2010–2011

steps.action: Fit the Shao-Raupach profile to q(z), integrate to Q, take the upwind-downwind PM10 flux divergence as F, and compute k_ss = F_PM10/Q_total (method 1).
steps.quote: we calculated the k factor that is calculated with sediment samplers

steps.action: Mount DustTrak PM10 monitors at 0.5, 1 and 2 m and a 5-m anemometer tower at both sites in September 2014.
steps.quote: The DustTraks were attached to masts with inlets at heights 0.5 m, 1 m and 2 m from the surface

steps.action: Record aerosol and wind data during two natural intense wind events.
steps.quote: The aerosol concentration (DustTrak) and meteorological measurements were performed during two intense wind events.

steps.action: Infer friction velocity and aerodynamic roughness height from the anemometer profiles with the law of the wall.
steps.quote: We used the law of the wall to compute aerodynamic roughness height from the cup anemometer measurements.

steps.action: Revise the Li et al. (2010) erodibility method by refitting its data with impact-hole size alone, because a penetrometer could not be used on crust-less sand.
steps.quote: the data from Li et al. (2010) were reanalyzed using only the size of an impact hole

steps.action: Check the airgun premise: impact-hole areas are compared with Li et al.'s Mojave values, and the threshold is compared with Bagnold's loose-sand expression.
steps.quote: The average values of A at our sites are consistent with those that Li et al. (2010) reported

steps.action: Compute F with the Gillette-Walker gradient method; because the concurrent trap samples were lost, model Q with Gillette and Passi (1988) and compute k_dt = F/Q_mod (method 2).
steps.quote: we were not able to use the data because the samples were lost during transit

steps.action: Measure clay content of topsoil at both sites and compute the k expected from the Marticorena-Bergametti clay relation.
steps.quote: with values from the empirical relationship developed by Marticorena and Bergametti (1995)

steps.action: Compare the airgun thresholds (0.167 and 0.109 m/s) with literature; the Spaarwater value falls below the reported minimum.
steps.quote: the value at Spaarwater is unreasonably lower than the minimum value

steps.action: Replace the Spaarwater threshold with the Bagnold value (about 0.17 m/s) from grain size, then report Q_mod, z0 and k_dt for both sites.
steps.quote: we used the grain size data from sediments in Spaarwater to calculate

steps.action: Compare k from method 1 (BSNE) and method 2 (DustTrak) at Spaarwater and find them similar.
steps.quote: the k factors at Spaarwater measured with the two different methods are quite similar

steps.action: Compare thresholds and k values with published values from Owens Lake, Chihuahuan Desert, Spain, Niger, Mono Lake and west Texas.
steps.quote: we compare our results to results from other studies with similar soil texture

steps.action: Compare field k with the clay-based estimates; the difference is judged inconsequential given the scatter in Gillette's data.
steps.quote: the difference between our estimates of k factor from method 1 and method 2 and those produced using estimated clay content is inconsequential

steps.action: Propagate each k into the Bhattachan et al. (2013) regional emission estimate; the three field k values give 1.36-1.80 Tg/yr, a 28% range.
steps.quote: the range of uncertainty among the three different field-derived k factors used in this study

steps.action: Conclude that either field method is appropriate for estimating k in sandy soils like the southern Kalahari.
steps.quote: any of the methods described here are appropriate for estimation of k for sandy soils

no; k is inferred from measured or modeled F and Q

found: natural field sites and two natural wind events
two methods agree within order of magnitude and 28% in emission; consistent with clay-based k
both methods judged appropriate for sandy soils

end.claim: Two field methods (BSNE flux divergence, and DustTrak gradient flux with modeled Q) give k for Kalahari sand within the same order of magnitude, consistent with texture-based estimates, so either is appropriate for estimating k in sandy soils.

decisive_move.sentence: The comparison of k from the BSNE divergence method and the DustTrak method at Spaarwater; without it there is no basis for calling the methods interchangeable.

gates.evidence: Method 1 data were collected in 2010-2011, years before the 2014 DustTrak experiment, and no hypothesis is stated as directing acquisition. The methods could have disagreed by an order of magnitude, but no agreement criterion was fixed in advance; 'quite similar' and 'inconsequential' are judged after the fact. Nothing was registered.

imports.item: DustTrak 8533 optical aerosol monitor for PM10 concentrations
LS 13320 Beckman Coulter laser particle size analyzer
law of the wall with von Karman constant to infer friction velocity and roughness height

novelty_claims.quote: In fact, there are no studies that use two different methods at the same location to calculate k.
we are not aware of any other studies that have compared the k factor using these two methods

limits: Sub-claim: k for southern Kalahari sand is about 3-5 x 10^-4 per metre (Spaarwater k_ss 4.30 x 10^-4 +/- 2.76 x 10^-4; k_dt reported with uncertainty), status estimate_with_resolution. The two methods are not concurrent: method 1 uses 2010-2011 monthly trap data, method 2 a single 2014 day per site. Method 2 uses modeled Q (Gillette-Passi), not measured Q, because the samples were lost, so it is not a fully measured F/Q estimate. The reported values are inconsistent: the text gives Spaarwater k_dt = 3.26 x 10^-4 and k_ss = 4.51 x 10^-4, while Table 1 lists k_dt = 4.51 x 10^-4 and Table 2 gives k_ss = 4.30 x 10^-4. The Table 1 caption cites Gillette and Passi (1998) and Equation 7, though the text uses Gillette and Passi (1988) and Equation 8. The claim that BSNE trap efficiency cancels in the divergence method is argued, not tested. The 28% agreement is computed on upscaled emission, which is linear in k, so it is equivalent to the spread in k; no agreement threshold is stated. Only one site was measured with both methods. Data are available only on request. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence was coded, although the acknowledgments mention reviewer comments. Inference: the long-term BSNE data appear to come from earlier fieldwork (2010-2011) not designed for this comparison.

disagreements.support: Cites observed past land-use and drought reactivation of Kalahari dunes and future-scenario studies; no new evidence of its own.
disagreements.quote: some suggest that the Kalahari dunes will remain in a stable vegetated state because of limited wind power in the region

disagreements.target: Li et al. (2010) airgun erodibility method (as revised here) at Spaarwater
disagreements.support: The airgun threshold at Spaarwater fell below the literature minimum and was replaced by the Bagnold value.
disagreements.quote: the value at Spaarwater is unreasonably lower than the minimum value

disagreements.target: Bhattachan et al. (2013) regional dust emission estimate (0.42 Tg/yr from clay-based k)
disagreements.support: Field-derived k values give 1.36-1.80 Tg/yr, higher than the earlier estimate but within typical order-of-magnitude uncertainty.
disagreements.quote: the dust flux calculated using k from the two field methods in this study are greater than those of Bhattachan et al. (2013)

disagreements.target: Marticorena and Bergametti (1995) clay-content relationship for k
disagreements.support: Field k values are about three times the clay-based values; the authors judge this inconsequential against Gillette's within-soil scatter.
disagreements.quote: vary slightly from our field-based estimates of the k factor
